title: an-inference-call-logs-that-it-started
intention: Starting an inference call leaves a record on disk, so the sole path to every inference host stops being the one boundary in the system that crosses silently.
why:
AKIEN, 2026-08-18, naming this example himself: 'every single everyting is supposed to log major boundry crossings and state changes. that doesn't mean every function call, or every heartbeat from the ground loop... but STARTING AN INFERENCE CALL SURE SHOULD.' MEASURED THE SAME DAY, and the measurement moved the build rather than confirming the plan: `grep -c 'emit(' cairn/devices/inference_domain/` returns ZERO — not few, none — and not from oversight. emit() lives on DiagnosticBase, DiagnosticBase is composed onto BaseDevice, and inference_domain HAS NO CLASS: domain.py, host.py and route.py are modules of functions, so resolve(), ollama_resolver() and route() have no `self` for emit() to be a method on. The parent's cast phrase 'inference_domain gains an emitter' is therefore unsatisfiable as written.

THE LIVED SYMPTOM. host.py's resolver shakes a nest of routes, dials the survivors cheapest-first, walks to the next rung on HostUnreachable, and refuses loudly when the walk exhausts. All of that happens today with no record. A mind arriving at an inference red has a traceback and nothing about the route that produced it — which host was tried, in what order, what each one said — so it re-explores by hand, and that is the exact cost diagnostic_inspector's charter exists to remove.

AND IT IS A GAP IN THE DOMAIN'S OWN CLAIM, which is the sharper half. The charter says 'the meter IS the learning surface' and the domain records every call in inference_calls — including, since 2026-08-18, the ones that RAISE. So the domain already knows what each call COST and cannot say what it DID. The trail is the second half of a record the store opened.
traces_to: Law 7 first — 'errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces'. The inference path is the surface where a red is least readable from anywhere else: host.py walks a nest of rungs cheapest-first and refuses when the walk exhausts, and today that whole walk happens with no record, so a mind arriving at an inference red has the traceback and nothing about the route that produced it. Law 3 second, and it is the sharper one: the domain's whole point is that the meter turns calls into evidence, and its charter says so ('the meter IS the learning surface'). A crossing that leaves no record is an observation not taken. Also Telos 1 by the parent's line — the yield report can say what inference COST and cannot say what it DID.

falsifier.proves_green:
code-seam invariant, transcribed onto this node: PROVED, and feeds-back-to-origin-on-failure (Laws 3 + 8).

PROVE GATE — the tester runs proofs beside each component this touches: cairn/tools/base/proofs/ for the module-scoped trail, and cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/ for the call sites. CHECK-TYPE is deterministic-and-on-disk, and the tooth a hollow build could not pass is stated as a bound rather than a suggestion: an inference call is driven through resolve() with a stub resolver against a TEMP roots table, and the record is then found BY OPENING THE FILE at log_path('inference_domain', 0, roots) and parsing the line — never by reading the return value of emit(), never by asking a mock what it received. A hollow build that shapes a record and drops it passes every object-side assertion and fails this one.

SECOND TOOTH, THE AGREEMENT CLAUSE: over one driven window, miss records in the trail are counted against verdict='miss' rows the same run landed in inference_calls, and the two must be equal. This is what the proof cannot write both sides of — the store half is written by resolve()'s existing path.

ISOLATION is set_diagnostic_roots / a temp roots table, not a hand-wired receiver: diagnostic.py's own docstring says a proof wanting isolation should reach for the roots seam because wiring a receiver 'would quietly prove the receiver instead of the default', and the default IS the mechanism under test. The instance seal (child 4) is the belt to that braces.

WATCH GATE: WATCHME(an_inference_call_logs_that_it_started), spec in `watchme`, probe armed at the berth named there before the crossing.

PARENT GATE: this child proves before every-boundary-crossing-lands-in-the-logs-tree crosses PROVED.
falsifier.proves_red:
FALSIFIER, refined from /intent's first cut and tightened at the second clause: DONE when (a) a real inference call — not a fixture — leaves a record at ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0/diagnostics.jsonl, read back BY OPENING THE FILE and never by asking the object whether it logged; (b) that record names the host that answered and whether the call was a hit or a miss; and (c) THE TRAIL AND THE METER AGREE — the count of miss records in the trail equals the count of verdict='miss' rows landed in the inference_calls table over the same window. Clause (c) is the one that makes this falsifiable rather than merely satisfiable: the domain already records every call in a store, so the trail is a SECOND record of the same events, and two records of one event that disagree are worse than one record (Law 7). It also means the proof cannot pass by writing its own evidence — the store is written by resolve(), not by the trail.

WRONG INTENT IF, and both directions are named because the grain can fail either way: a record per rung of the nest walk turns an ordinary cheapest-first resolution into what reads as three failures; a record only at ANSWER leaves the refusals — the case the logging exists FOR — invisible. Either would mean the seam shipped and the picture did not.

HORIZON: the next inference call the system actually makes, which needs no clock and no new instrument — the domain is the sole path, so any real traffic tests this. Bounded above by the parent's own crossing: every-boundary-crossing-lands-in-the-logs-tree cannot cross PROVED before its children, and this is child (2).

how:
TWO points were asserted wrapped at /intent and one of them was not.

WRAPPED AND HOLDING: the device-ness question. /intent settled it — inference_domain does not become a BaseDevice to obtain logging, because its own charter defers the runtime face on independent grounds and DiagnosticBase derives everything it needs from an address a module also has. That is a real resolution with a reason, not a deferral.

NOT WRAPPED, AND IT IS THE GRAIN. /intent's falsifier says a record must name 'which host answered and whether the answer was a hit or a miss', and its wrong-intent clause says a record per rung of the nest walk would make an ordinary cheapest-first resolution look like three failures. Those two are in tension and I did not notice at birth: host.py's resolver WALKS rungs on HostUnreachable, so 'which host answered' is only knowable by observing the walk, and observing the walk is the thing the wrong-intent clause warns against. The resolution, and it is a decision this cast makes rather than defers: ONE record per inference call at the outcome, carrying the host that answered and the rungs it had to walk past as a VALUE on that record — not one record per rung. A walk is one crossing with a path, not three crossings. This is what keeps 'starting an inference call' a single readable line and still answers 'why was it slow'.

MEASURED FIRST, and the measurement moved the approach off the one the parent assumed. `grep -c 'emit(' cairn/devices/inference_domain/` returns 0 — not 'few', none — and the reason is structural rather than an oversight: emit() lives on DiagnosticBase, DiagnosticBase is composed onto BaseDevice, and inference_domain HAS NO CLASS. domain.py, host.py and route.py are modules of functions; `resolve()`, `ollama_resolver()` and `route()` are where the crossings happen and none of them has a `self`. So the parent's phrase 'inference_domain gains an emitter' cannot be satisfied by adding emit sites — there is nothing to add them to.

THE DEVICE-NESS QUESTION, ANSWERED THE CHEAP WAY. The expensive answer is to give inference_domain a BaseDevice class. Its own charter refuses that on independent grounds — 'the BaseDevice introspection FACE and bus-fronting are the runtime face — deferred until a prober/runtime pulls them' — and building the device face in order to obtain logging would be building it for a reason that is not its reason. The cheap answer is that DiagnosticBase already derives EVERYTHING it needs from `type(self)`: the device name from `type(self).__module__` through `address.component_of_module`, the source from `type(self).__name__`, the instance from a default of 0. A module has all three facts in `__name__`. So the seam is a module-scoped trail on the floor — a small DiagnosticBase whose device and source come from a module address instead of a class address — held at module level and emitted through. It composes the default receiver, the held-not-lost semantics, the record shape and `set_diagnostic_roots` (the proof-isolation seam) without rebuilding one of them.

THE GRAIN IS ALREADY WRITTEN. The charter names the crossings: RECEIVE -> CANONICALIZE -> lookup -> (hit) VERIFY -> ANSWER, or (miss) METER -> RESOLVE -> RECORD -> ANSWER. Akien's 'starting an inference call' is the miss branch's RESOLVE — the point where it actually leaves for a host — and the hit branch is the interesting negative: a cache hit is a boundary NOT crossed, and saying so is what makes the trail readable against the meter it already keeps.
